title: Rava, Grandson of Rav Pappi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, beginning of chapter 1, folio 1b. Hyman writes that it seems the reading should be “son of R' Pappi,” and that he is R' Ba son of R' Pappi.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Guggenheimer digital text of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:1 fully writes Rava bar bereih deRav Papai, a grandson of Rav Papai, supporting Rav for the father-title abbreviation in Hyman’s proposed reading. Hyman’s change from grandson to son and identification with Rabbi Ba are tentative proposals, not a genealogy admitted from this comparison.

The whole Guggenheimer Shabbat 1:1 paragraph has Rava the grandson of Rav Papai. That does not supply full titles for Hyman’s conjectural Pappi and Ba, rendered R'. The existing note’s claim that the grandson passage supports the proposed father title is retained verbatim as earlier commentary and is qualified here: no such title transfer is adopted. Hyman’s “it seems/should read” and proposed son identification remain attributed, without a genealogy binding.
